correctness.rationale: The proof establishes the normalized kernel and exact projection norm, derives a nonnegative increment from an independent sign, identifies opposite signs of neighboring kernel values as the only contributors, proves all four quartic roots lie in distinct grid cells unless aligned, and carries out a positive Pell descent to two exponentially growing solution orbits. Actual verify_quartic.py uses independent combinatorial evaluation and exact integer arithmetic; its finite checks do not replace the analytical infinite proof.

value.rationale: The finding resolves a natural endpoint norm stabilization question with a two-term exact increment rule and a per-dimension arithmetic plateau test, proves at most logarithmically many possible quartic plateaus, and relates exact Fourier projection stability to rare integral Krawtchouk roots. The natural invariant is the projection norm across adjacent Boolean dimensions; the result is not simply a small table or a generic asymptotic.
